condition: Find products that are similar in their purpose, features, and the needs they address, even when their descriptions use different terminology.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Brand is a product attribute reachable via product. Brand can indicate product family or manufacturer style, providing a weak proxy for purpose/features, but brand alone does not capture purpose, features, or needs and is confounded by diverse product lines under one brand. Limited direct evidence for similarity in purpose/features/needs.

product.category is a direct attribute of the starting product table. Category can group items by broad purpose or type, providing a weak proxy for similarity in purpose/features/needs, but it is coarse and does not capture nuanced feature or need overlap or terminology differences.

The signal is product.description from the product table. Description text can provide purpose, features, and needs terminology, but similarity based on different wording requires semantic matching beyond raw description alone. It offers weak, indirect evidence for finding similar products.

The signal is product.title from the product table with no joins. Title can provide a weak semantic cue about purpose/features, but alone it is a single short text field and does not capture description, category, brand, or review-derived usage signals needed to judge similarity across different terminology.

review.summary is a review-level text attribute on review. It can provide weak semantic cues about a product’s purpose/features via the review’s wording, but it is indirect, noisy, and not a product attribute; similarity must be inferred from many reviews and is confounded by reviewer language. Path is review only, with no link to product attributes beyond review.product_id, so evidence for product similarity is weak.

The signal is customer.customer_name reachable from customer only. The user condition requires product similarity by purpose/features/needs, which needs product attributes and review content. Customer name provides no product or review information and no path to product or review, so it cannot support the condition.

The signal is product.price from product. Price is a numeric cost attribute and does not capture purpose, features, or needs addressed, nor does it provide semantic similarity of descriptions. No path to review text or product description features is used, so it cannot indicate similarity in purpose/features/needs despite different terminology.

The signal is review.rating from review alone. Rating provides no product purpose, features, or needs information and does not connect to product attributes or description terminology. No evidence for similarity in purpose/features/needs.

The signal is review.review_text from the review table alone. It provides only the review text attribute with no path to product or customer, so it cannot link reviews to products or establish similarity between products. No product attributes or relationships are included, so the signal gives no evidence for finding products similar in purpose, features, or needs.

review.review_time is a timestamp on a review row. It provides no information about product purpose, features, or needs, nor about similarity between products. The path starts and ends at review with no link to product attributes or description terminology, so it cannot support the condition.

The signal is review.verified from the review table alone. Verified indicates whether a review is from a verified purchase, which provides no information about product purpose, features, or needs, nor about similarity between products. No path connects to product attributes or description terminology, so the signal cannot support finding similar products.

condition: Find products that appeal to similar groups of customers based on their purchasing and reviewing behavior, even if the products belong to different categories.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Signal is customer.customer_name from customer table alone. No product linkage, no review linkage, no purchasing or reviewing behavior. Cannot identify products or customer groups, so provides no evidence for products appealing to similar customer groups across categories.

The signal is product.brand from product alone. It provides no information about customers, purchasing or reviewing behavior, and cannot link products to similar customer groups or across categories. No relationship to review or customer is used.

The signal is product.category from product alone. The condition requires identifying products that appeal to similar customer groups based on purchasing and reviewing behavior across categories. Category provides no information about customers, reviews, or cross-category customer overlap, so it cannot support the requested similarity.

The signal is product.description from product alone. It provides no information about customers, purchasing or reviewing behavior, and cannot link products via shared customer groups. No relationship to review or customer is used, so it cannot support finding products that appeal to similar customer groups.

The signal is product.price from product alone. Price is a product attribute with no path to review or customer, so it provides no evidence about customer groups, purchasing or reviewing behavior, or cross-category appeal based on shared customers. The condition requires customer-based similarity; price alone cannot indicate similar customer groups.

The signal is product.title from product alone. It provides only the product name with no customer, review, or purchase behavior linkage, so it cannot indicate which customer groups appeal to the product or enable similarity across categories.

The signal is review.rating from review alone. It provides no product or customer linkage and no way to compare groups of customers across products, so it cannot support finding products that appeal to similar customer groups.

The signal is review.review_text from review alone. It provides only the text of a single review with no product, customer, or linking information in the path, so it cannot identify products, customers, or groups, nor relate products across categories.

review.review_time is a timestamp on a review row. It provides no information about which customers bought or reviewed which products, nor about customer groups or cross-category similarity. The signal is isolated to review and does not connect to product or customer attributes needed to infer similar customer groups.

The signal is review.summary from review alone. It provides only a textual summary of a single review with no link to product identity, customer identity, or any cross-product aggregation. Without product_id, customer_id, or any relationship traversal, it cannot identify products, group customers, or compare purchasing/reviewing behavior across products or categories. Therefore it offers no evidence for finding products that appeal to similar customer groups.

The signal is review.verified from the review table alone. It provides no product or customer linkage and no information about groups of customers, purchasing or reviewing behavior, or cross-category similarity. No path connects to product or customer, so it cannot support the condition.

condition: Find customer reviews that provide detailed, credible, and useful insights into a product's strengths, weaknesses, and real-world performance.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: review.review_text is the primary content carrier for detailed, credible, and useful insights about a product's strengths, weaknesses, and real-world performance. Starting from review, the text field directly provides the narrative evidence needed to assess usefulness, though credibility and detail level still require interpretation beyond the raw text alone.

review.summary is a short headline from the review table. It can hint at sentiment or a key point but is too brief to convey detailed, credible, useful insights about strengths, weaknesses, and real-world performance; the full review_text is needed for depth.

The signal is customer.customer_name from the customer table with no path to review or product. Customer name alone provides no evidence about review detail, credibility, usefulness, or product strengths/weaknesses/performance. No relationship to review attributes such as rating, review_text, review_time, summary, verified, nor to product attributes.

The signal is product.brand from product. Brand alone does not indicate whether a review is detailed, credible, or useful, nor does it describe strengths, weaknesses, or real-world performance. No review attributes or review content are involved, so the signal provides no evidence for the condition.

The signal is product.category from product. Category alone does not indicate whether a review is detailed, credible, useful, or discusses strengths, weaknesses, or real-world performance. No review attributes or review-product linkage is used.

The signal is product.description from product. The user condition requires detailed, credible, useful customer reviews about strengths, weaknesses, and real-world performance. Product description is a product attribute, not a review attribute, and provides no evidence about review detail, credibility, or usefulness, nor about real-world performance from customers.

The signal is product.price from product. Price is a product attribute and does not describe review content, credibility, detail, or real-world performance insights. No path connects price to review attributes like review_text, rating, verified, or review_time, so it provides no evidence for detailed, credible, useful customer reviews about strengths, weaknesses, and performance.

The signal is product.title from product. The user condition requires detailed, credible, useful insights about strengths, weaknesses, and real-world performance from customer reviews. Product title alone provides no review content, credibility, or performance insight, and does not connect to review attributes like rating, review_text, verified, or review_time. No evidence for the condition.

The signal is only review.rating from the review table. Rating alone does not indicate detail, credibility, usefulness, or coverage of strengths, weaknesses, and real-world performance. No review_text, summary, verified, review_time, or product/customer context is included, so the signal provides no evidence for the condition.

review.review_time is a timestamp attribute on review with no path to product strengths, weaknesses, or performance content. It provides no evidence about detail, credibility, or usefulness of insights.

The signal is review.verified alone. Verified indicates purchase verification but provides no information about detail, credibility of content, or usefulness regarding strengths, weaknesses, or real-world performance. No review_text, rating, summary, review_time, or product/customer attributes are included, so the signal cannot support the condition.

condition: Find products that offer particularly good value for money by balancing affordability, perceived quality, and customer satisfaction.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: review.summary is a free-text field on review. It can provide qualitative cues about perceived quality and satisfaction, but it is not a structured measure of affordability, price, or quality, and it is not aggregated. Alone it gives only weak, indirect evidence for value-for-money balancing.

customer.customer_name is a name string with no link to affordability, quality, or satisfaction. The path starts at customer and provides only the name, which does not capture price, perceived quality, or customer satisfaction for products.

The signal is product.brand from product. Brand alone provides no information about affordability, perceived quality, or customer satisfaction. No price, rating, review_text, or other quality/satisfaction attributes are included, and no path to review or customer is used. Therefore it cannot support the value-for-money condition.

The signal is product.category alone. Category provides only a grouping label with no information about affordability, perceived quality, or customer satisfaction. It does not connect to price, rating, review_text, verified, or any customer data, so it cannot support the value-for-money condition.

The signal is product.description from product. Description is a free-text marketing field with no numeric or structured quality, price, or satisfaction information. It provides no evidence for affordability, perceived quality, or customer satisfaction, and cannot support value-for-money assessment.

The signal is product.price alone. The condition requires balancing affordability, perceived quality, and customer satisfaction. Price alone provides no information about perceived quality or customer satisfaction, and cannot by itself indicate value for money. No evidence of quality or satisfaction is reachable from this signal.

The signal is product.title from product alone. Title provides no information about affordability, perceived quality, or customer satisfaction. No price, rating, review_text, or other value-related attributes are included, and the path contains only product with no joins to review or customer. Therefore it cannot support the value-for-money condition.

The signal is review.rating from review alone. It provides perceived quality/customer satisfaction but gives no product affordability information and no product identity linkage in the signal definition. Without product price or a path to product, it cannot support balancing affordability with perceived quality and satisfaction for products.

The signal is review.review_text from review alone. It provides only free-form text with no affordability, quality, or satisfaction metrics, and no link to product price, brand, category, or customer. No path connects to product attributes or aggregated satisfaction, so it cannot support value-for-money balancing.

review.review_time is a timestamp on the review table with no path to product price, brand, category, description, title, or to review rating, review_text, summary, verified. The condition requires affordability, perceived quality, and customer satisfaction, which need product price and review rating/text signals. Review time alone provides no evidence for value for money.

The signal is review.verified from the review table alone. It provides no product affordability, quality, or customer satisfaction information and does not connect to product attributes or aggregate customer sentiment. It cannot support identifying products with good value for money.

condition: Find customers who have similar preferences and expectations, as reflected in the products they review, the opinions they express, and the aspects of products they care about.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: The signal is only customer.customer_name from the customer table with no path to review or product. It provides no information about reviewed products, opinions, or cared aspects, so it cannot support finding customers with similar preferences and expectations.

The signal is product.brand reachable from product only. The user condition requires customers with similar preferences and expectations reflected in products they review, opinions they express, and aspects they care about. Starting from product and using brand provides no customer linkage and no review content or opinion aspects, so it cannot evidence customer similarity.

The signal is product.category reachable from product only. The user condition requires customers with similar preferences and expectations as reflected in products they review, opinions they express, and aspects they care about. Starting from a product and using its category provides no connection to customers, review opinions, or aspects, so it cannot support the condition.

Signal is product.description from product table. Starting entity is customer. Path is product only, with no link from customer to product. No review join is specified, so the signal cannot be reached from customer and provides no evidence about customers preferences, opinions, or aspects they care about.

The signal is product.price reachable from product via path product. The user condition requires customers with similar preferences and expectations as reflected in products they review, opinions they express, and aspects they care about. Price alone from product provides no customer linkage and no opinion or aspect information, so it cannot support identifying similar customers.

Signal is product.title from product table with no path to customer. The condition requires customers linked via reviews and their expressed opinions/aspects. Product title alone provides no customer linkage and no review content, so it cannot support finding customers with similar preferences.

The signal is review.rating from review alone. It provides only a single review's rating with no customer identity, no product context, and no textual opinions or aspects. It cannot link reviews to customers or products, so it cannot support finding customers with similar preferences, expectations, opinions, or cared-about aspects.

The signal is review.review_text from review alone. It provides the opinion text for a single review but does not connect reviews to customers or products, nor does it capture product attributes or aspects. No path links to customer or product, so it cannot identify customers with similar preferences or expectations.

review.review_time is a timestamp on a review row. It provides no information about product preferences, expressed opinions, or cared aspects, and does not connect reviews to other customers or products beyond the review itself. No evidence for similarity of preferences or expectations.

The signal is review.summary from review alone. It provides a single review's summary text but no link to the customer or product, and no way to compare across reviews or customers. The condition requires identifying customers with similar preferences across products, opinions, and cared aspects, which needs customer identity and product context. The signal lacks customer_id, product_id, and any cross-review aggregation, so it cannot support similarity between customers.

The signal is review.verified alone, with no path to customer or product. It provides no information about which customers reviewed which products, the opinions expressed, or product aspects they care about, so it cannot support finding customers with similar preferences and expectations.
